exposure: type of counseling (obstetrics, pediatrics, social services)
outcome: selection of pregnancy termination method (induction of labor (IOL) or dilation and evacuation (D&E))
cohort: The participants were women who experienced pregnancy termination for fetal anomaly, intrauterine fetal demise, or premature previable rupture at 17-24 weeks of gestation.
finding: Patient characteristics, medical factors, and type of counseling were significantly associated with the selection between D&E and IOL for anomalous pregnancies in the second trimester.
mod_finding: Women of color, those with lower education and employment, and those with specific medical factors (intrauterine fetal demise, premature previable rupture, prior substance use disorder) or counseling types had higher odds of selecting induction of labor compared to dilation and evacuation.
